text:
alex: FYI — I hacked an 'autosignal' TTL prototype that nudges span TTLs up/down based on recent query pressure + an org cost budget. rough logic: low queries => cold-ttl 7d, high queries or SLA-tagged => promote to warm 30d.

maya: interesting. how do you define 'recent query pressure'? sliding window?

alex: yeah, a 24h sliding window per service+env, with exponential decay. threshold is percentile-based (p95 queries/sec across services) so noisy tenants don't force global change.

omar: how do we avoid oscillation during bursts? spikes could flip TTLs every hour.

alex: we debounce with hysteresis and cool-downs. rule: require sustained above-threshold for 6h to promote, and sustained below for 48h to demote. also cap promotions per-week.

jen: UX question — how would this show up in Console? we need visibility and override.

alex: Console -> TraceRetention page: show current policy per service, last-change, reason (auto-signal or manual), and button to pin TTL (manual override).

esther: any compliance implications? some customers need minimum retention.

alex: we always respect tenant minimums; autosignal can only increase TTL above the min, not reduce below. there's also an allowlist for 'never-demote' services.

ryan: rehydration cost is my main worry. If we promote cold->warm on query, are we going to backfill from GCS/S3 on every user query? expensive.

alex: plan is to do on-demand rehydrate only for query-heavy traces: when a query touches an archived trace, kick a background rehydrate job that prioritizes based on query frequency and returns immediate sampling results. less-than-interactive queries can async fetch.

omar: can we cache rehydrated prefixes/KV to avoid repeated backfills?

alex: yes, prefix cache + short-lived local bundle for 24-72h after rehydrate. that reduces repeated cold fetches for post-mortems.

jen: need a simple opt-in experience for teams: a checkbox "enable autosignal TTL" + cost cap slider in UI. default off for now.

alex: prototype config (for experimentation):
```yaml
service_ttl_autosignal:
  enabled: true
  query_window: 24h
  promote_threshold: 95pct
  promote_sustain: 6h
  demote_sustain: 48h
  warm_ttl: 30d
  cold_ttl: 7d
  per_service_weekly_promotions_limit: 2
  respect_tenant_min: true
  rehydrate_strategy: on_demand_priority
```

maya: what signals do we need from the telemetry pipeline? exporter-level counters? endpoint latencies?

alex: need: per-service query count, percentage of requests touching archived spans, cost-per-fetch estimate, and span-age distribution. OT span tags: `trace.service.name`, `env`, `retention.policy` (opt-in).

esther: add `compliance.level` tag so Private customers can opt-out of auto demotion.

ryan: rollout plan? feature flag + canary on low-risk orgs?

alex: v1 behind FF; canary set to internal + 5 beta tenants. collect metrics for 2 weeks then expand. will also expose a dashboard with: promotions/sec, rehydrate ops/sec, avg rehydrate latency, cost delta.

sre-bot: alert: storage-pressure high on us-west-2-cold-bucket (avg read-latency 1.8s). recommend limiting immediate promotions until mitigations in place. :warning:

omar: thanks bot — maybe add a global throttle: if cold-bucket read-latency > 1s, reduce automatic promotions by 80%.

alex: good call. I'll add a throttling rule tied to exporter health.

jen: next steps: 1) Alex to land prototype config + console stub; 2) Omar to design debounce/hysteresis math; 3) Maya to spec required pipeline counters; 4) Esther to validate compliance flags; 5) Ryan to configure FF + canary tenants.

alex: pinging owners in thread for visibility. TL;DR — autosignal TTL can reduce cost by demoting cold services while protecting hot ones, but we must handle oscillation, rehydrate cost, and console UX first. :nerd_face:
